web_evidence.title: The Rainmaker by John Grisham
web_evidence.note: The author's official site supplies an authorized Chapter One excerpt narrated by a participating 'I' discussing his father and decision to become a lawyer.

web_evidence.title: Writing Techniques in The Rainmaker
web_evidence.note: This structural study-guide entry, credited to Gale, explicitly identifies a first-person narrator, associates the voice with Rudy, and describes the novel's present-tense narration.

web_evidence.title: The Rainmaker Analysis
web_evidence.note: The analysis explicitly describes the novel's first-person narrative, identifies Rudy Baylor as narrator, and discusses the trial and other plot stages as presented through Rudy's narration.

person_note: The Goodreads evidence repeatedly exposes Rudy Baylor as a participating 'I' narrator across law school, client work, and litigation-related scenes. The official opening independently uses the same participating voice, while two whole-book structural sources explicitly identify Rudy's first-person narration. Generic second-person language in q00001 and q00018 is maxim-like rather than sustained address to a protagonist, and the speech, gnomic material, and Deck's embedded rules do not constitute competing narrative sections. No evidence of sustained third- or second-person base narration was found; the official excerpt's opening-only scope is offset by extensive interior quote evidence and whole-book structural descriptions.
